segments.title: Tape trouble at the start
segments.summary: DeParis says something went wrong with the recording and they will play it back.

segments.title: Cy Elliot and the Wolfscale brothers
segments.summary: DeParis recalls Cy Elliot, who looked like a stevedore but could play, and the Wolfscale brothers; the interviewer says Paul Barbarin mentioned them.

segments.title: Working with Sidney Bechet and Tommy Ladnier in Noble Sissle's band
segments.summary: DeParis, Bechet and Ladnier were in Sissle's band for two years in Paris; Bechet and Ladnier played only solo and swing choruses, not section work.

segments.title: First musical experience and instruments
segments.summary: He started in carnival bands, brass bands and medicine shows, on alto horn, bass horn and baritone, then trombone and a little saxophone in New Orleans.

segments.title: Teachers and learning from experience
segments.summary: He had teachers briefly but learned mostly from experience.

segments.title: First jobs on his father's small carnival
segments.summary: His first job was with his father on a gilly show, explained as a small carnival moving by boxcar; he stayed with his father through high school.

segments.title: Organizing his own band and bringing Sidney to Philadelphia
segments.summary: He formed his own band, led Billy Mack's Merrymakers at 18, and brought his brother Sidney to Philadelphia.

segments.title: Best jobs: carnival money versus prestige places
segments.summary: The most money was in carnival days; he also played prestige places in France and the London Palladium, plus medicine shows, circuses, vaudeville and tab shows.

segments.title: Replacing Tricky Sam in Duke Ellington's band
segments.summary: Ellington's was a band played strictly from the paper; he took Tricky Sam's place and played his parts without the solos.

segments.title: Mutes and plunger use
segments.summary: He seldom uses a mute himself but used straight and cup mutes with Duke; he used a plunger when younger, as Sidney still does.

segments.title: Ending the tape
segments.summary: The interviewer says the tape is nearly finished and they decide to let it run off and rewind.
